findings.title: Use stored enabled state when deciding login-cache invalidation
findings.body: The original model passed here comes from getById(), which wraps organization-linked providers so that isEnabled() returns false while their organization (or the organization feature in the realm) is disabled. However, getForLogin() populates its cached ID set using the delegate's stored enabled state. For example, cache an enabled public organization provider, disable its organization, then change BROKER_PUBLIC to false. Both predicates here return false, so the cached login list is retained. Once the organization is enabled again, that now-private provider is still returned from the cache and displayed by OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean, which only rechecks isEnabled(). Compare the original and updated persisted provider states, rather than organization-aware enabled states, when deciding whether query membership changed.

findings.title: Register cleanup for the actual provider aliases
findings.body: The new test creates providers named idp-alias-0 through idp-alias-19, but every cleanup callback removes the literal alias "alias". The additional callback at line 425 has the same problem for idp-alias-20. These callbacks therefore do not remove the created providers and can fail with a not-found response during teardown. In particular, the realm-level providers survive organization cleanup and pollute subsequent tests or cause duplicate-alias failures on another run. Register each callback using the alias of the provider it created.
